meta_title: Server Profiles: Your Servers' Settings in VpnHood! MANAGER | VpnHood!
meta_description: Give all the servers of a farm the same settings with a server profile in VpnHood! MANAGER, the settings for a censored network and for a reverse proxy among them.
title: Server profiles
lead: A server profile holds the settings of your servers. Each server farm uses one, and VpnHood! MANAGER sends its settings to every server of the farm, so you change them in one place.
where_desc: Open [manager_settings] and select [manager_server_profiles]. Every project starts with a default profile, which a new server farm uses unless you choose another. The default profile can be neither renamed nor deleted, and no profile that a farm uses can be deleted.
where_farm: A farm's page in [manager_server_farms] names its profile under [manager_server_profile]: select the name to open the profile, or edit it to give the farm another one.
settings_card: A profile's page sets the common ones under [manager_general], [manager_network_filter] and [manager_tracking]. For any other, select [manager_advanced_edit]: it shows the servers' settings as JSON, under the same names as on a standalone server, which Server configuration explains one by one. Change them and select [manager_ok].
shot_alt: VpnHood! MANAGER's Server Profile card: Advanced edit marked at its top, above the General panel's settings and the Network Filter and Tracking panels
shot_caption: A profile's page: the common settings in their panels, each setting with its own pencil, and [manager_advanced_edit] for all the others
settings_send: MANAGER sends the new settings to every server of the farms that use the profile.
settings_refused: MANAGER refuses the few settings it sets for each server itself, and its message names the setting. [setting_udp_endpoints] and [setting_quic_endpoints] take only [json_empty_list], which turns UDP or QUIC off on the profile's servers: their ports are each server's own, set in its access points.
settings_dropped: MANAGER keeps only the settings it knows and drops any other as you save, a misspelled name too, so open [manager_advanced_edit] again to check yours.
netfilter_desc: [manager_network_filter] decides which destinations your users can reach through the profile's servers. Each field sets one server setting, which Server configuration explains in full.
netfilter_alt: VpnHood! MANAGER's Network Filter panel: Block IpV6, Include Local Network, Block SMTP (Port 25), Block TCP Ports, Block UDP Ports, Kernel Include and Exclude IP Addresses, and Include and Exclude IP Addresses
netfilter_caption: A profile's Network Filter with its defaults: port 25 blocked, and nothing else
nf_block_ipv6: Blocks IPv6 on the profile's servers and tells the apps they carry none. Sets [setting_block_ipv6].
nf_local_network: Lets your users reach the servers' own addresses and their networks that are not public. Turn it on only where your users should reach them. Sets [setting_include_local_network].
nf_smtp: Stops your users from sending mail straight to mail servers, which gets a server's IP address reported as a spam source; mail apps send on ports 587 and 465 and keep working. On by default, it keeps port 25 in [manager_block_tcp_ports].
nf_tcp_ports: The TCP ports your users cannot reach, as ports or ranges separated by commas, such as [ports_example_manager]. Sets [setting_block_tcp_ports].
nf_udp_ports: The UDP ports your users cannot reach, written the same way. Sets [setting_block_udp_ports].
nf_kernel_include: The only destinations the apps' VPN adapters capture on the device; the rest goes outside the VPN. Filtering on the device is faster than with [manager_include_ips] but takes only a short list: a long one can make devices fail. Sets [setting_adapter_include_ip_ranges].
nf_kernel_exclude: Destinations the apps' VPN adapters leave outside the VPN. Sets [setting_adapter_exclude_ip_ranges].
nf_include: The only destinations the servers route. Sets [setting_include_ip_ranges].
nf_exclude: Destinations the servers do not route. Sets [setting_exclude_ip_ranges].
censored_desc: On a network that blocks VPN servers, a farm's profile gives all of its servers the settings for a censored network at once. Keep your server's IP address from being blocked explains each, and what it costs your users. In [manager_advanced_edit], set:
caption_censored: Cloak Mode for everyone, no UDP and no QUIC to the servers, and your users' QUIC dropped
censored_refused: MANAGER refuses [setting_allow_quic_packet] or [setting_allow_udp_packet] off while [setting_allow_tcp_packet] is on, as the servers would carry them anyway. It refuses [setting_allow_tcp_packet] and [setting_allow_tcp_forwarding] both off too, which leaves TCP no way through.
censored_minimum: To turn away probes too, set [manager_min_client_protocol] under [manager_general] to [min_protocol_proof], but only once your users' apps are on VpnHood 9.1 or later: older apps then cannot connect. Turn away probes explains it.
proxy_desc: Your servers trust Cloudflare to name each user's address. Behind another reverse proxy, open [manager_advanced_edit] and add the settings that Your users' addresses shows.
next_domain: Use your own domain with a trusted certificate
next_proxy: Send every app through a reverse proxy
